title: Introducing CARaL: Copyright Anxiety, Resilience and Leadership
content:
Many of you will know that Chris and I have been working for some time on research into Copyright Anxiety and Legal Chill. Therefore we are really excited to launch a new collaboration this autumn with the author, coach and trainer, Helen Rimmer. Helen is the author of the Facet book The Kind Librarian and her work on leadership and compassion really struck a chord with our findings that were emerging from the copyright anxiety research.

What’s CARaL all about?

CARaL: Copyright Anxiety, Resilience and Leadership is a new four-part online programme exploring something that traditional copyright training rarely addresses: the emotional, cultural and leadership impact of copyright work.

Copyright is a technical subject, but it is also felt emotionally. The fear of getting something wrong can lead to anxiety, over-checking, unnecessary escalation and what we’re calling “Legal Chill” – where over-caution begins to become a barrier to access, innovation and creativity.

title: Webinar 87: Transnational Education
content:
Our next webinar will take place on Friday 25th September from 11am-12pm and will be a closed webinar for the higher education community, operating under Chatham House rules.

As an increasing number of universities move into transnational education (TNE) partnerships, library support for TNE has become a recent hot topic of conversation! Many of you expressed a wish for a coming-together of the community on this matter. So, whether your TNE partnerships are well-established, or you’re taking your first steps into this area of service provision, we hope you will come along.

Our main speakers will be Greg Ince from Jisc (Transnational Education Licensing) and Alison Davidson (University of Liverpool). Greg brings his wealth of experience in supporting HE librarians to navigate the licensing issues around TNE. Alison provides the librarian’s perspective, based on her own recent experience of mapping the long-standing TNE partnerships at her university, in order to clarify what support the library can provide for new partnerships. Diane Crawford-Leighton (University of Exeter) will kick things off with a summary of the findings from her recent survey.
